According to the latest report from Counterpoint Research, despite an overall industry slowdown, Apple iPhone shipments still grew 3% year-on-year, setting a new historical high with a 20% share of global smartphone shipments. Details are as follows.

The lowest level for a second quarter since 2013

Counterpoint Research said that during the second quarter of 2026, Samsung led the global smartphone market with a 24% shipment share, followed by Apple with 20% (a historical high for that quarter), Xiaomi with 12%, OPPO with 11%, and vivo with 8%.

Compared with the same period last year, Samsung's market share rose by 4 percentage points, Apple's rose by 3 percentage points, vivo's rose by 1 percentage point, while Xiaomi's fell by 2 percentage points and OPPO's fell by 1 percentage point. The combined share of other manufacturers dropped from 28% to 26%.

Counterpoint pointed out that Samsung returned to the top of the global smartphone sell-in rankings in the second quarter of 2026, after Apple had led in the first quarter thanks to strong demand for the iPhone 17.

As for the second quarter of 2026, although Apple was the only major OEM that did not raise prices, Samsung benefited from strong demand for the Galaxy S26 series, improved product supply, and more aggressive promotional strategies, resulting in faster growth.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects "global smartphone shipments for the full year to decline by about 14%, with the global memory shortage expected to persist until 2027." The firm noted that until supply conditions improve, manufacturers will continue to cut low-margin models, adjust storage configurations, and rely more on refurbished and previous-generation products.
